findings.title: Null dereference when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the array is empty or null. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, so it throws a TypeError. This happens for any Meet booking where the host has no destination calendar, and several callers now pass `[]`. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which did not throw. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent is always undefined
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only reaches the fallback when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches for a calendar whose externalId equals that falsy value, which never matches. The old code fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. updateEvent now passes `calendarId: undefined`. deleteEvent still falls back to "primary". The same pattern is in deleteEvent at line 317. Fall back to the first destination calendar instead.

findings.title: hangoutLink patch uses a possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` can now be undefined because the insert falls back to "primary" while the patch does not. The patch after insert for Meet links then passes `calendarId: undefined`, which fails. It should use `selectedCalendar || "primary"`.

findings.title: Team destination calendars pushed into a null array, and the booking records only the first
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` then silently drops all team members' calendars. In addition, `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled as a side effect inside async map callbacks, which makes the ordering fragile. The booking row connects only `destinationCalendar[0]`.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops the organization select and changes error behavior
findings.body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug } }`. Code that relied on it may break. The rewrite also wraps every error as a 400 or 500 HttpError. This is unrelated to the PR and risky.

findings.title: Failed credential lookup silently skips the destination calendar
findings.body: When a destination's credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials` and the DB lookup also fails (for example the app has no slug), nothing is created and no error result is reported.
